name: Pallium India: palliative care expansion (HLI, 2026)
beneficiaries_note: The model's name: Pallium India: palliative care expansion (HLI, 2026).
summary: Builds palliative care services and opioid access in Indian states. The Happier Lives Institute's back-of-the-envelope range for Pallium India expanding into Karnataka (WELLBYs per $1,000), from its report; HLI gives only the range.

resources.title: HLI, Investigating three ways to reduce the global pain burden (2026), section 1 and Appendix B
resources.note: HLI publishes no public spreadsheet for this estimate: the model is built from the inputs and figures stated in the report's text, each quoted on its row. HLI calls it "a highly uncertain BOTEC" and plans a fuller report on palliative care.

resources.title: HLI, 2025 giving season charities update
resources.note: Quoted an earlier range for Pallium, 26 to 163 WELLBYs per $1,000, from analysis then in progress.

sections.title: HLI's range
sections.explainer: HLI models a hypothetical project: Pallium India helping Karnataka reach Kerala's palliative care coverage 5 to 8 years sooner, at about $200,000 a year for 5 years, reaching 1.1 to 3.2 million more patients over 10 years. Each patient gains 0.07 WELLBYs: pain down 4.5 points on a 0–10 scale, converted at a rate of 0.61 (Dupret et al. 2023) into 2.72 points of wellbeing, for the 15 days of care, plus 16.24% for each of 1.77 household members, times 0.51 for replication; then halved for the chance the project fails, with a 1% chance of an opioid overuse crisis. (Section 1 of the report gives the cost as $1–2 million over 5–10 years and 1.1–3.1 million patients; Appendix B's figures are used here.) Under HLI's theory of change the state government then delivers the care; that public money isn't counted as a contribution here, which flatters Pallium when credit by share of resources is on.

sections.title: Discounting
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not HLI's. HLI counts a year of better wellbeing the same whenever it comes. In our view, later years count less at the discount rate under Your values, as in GiveWell's models; the evaluator view sets the rate to 0, so HLI's figure is unchanged there.

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not the evaluator's: with credit by share of resources on, staff's pay below what they could earn elsewhere counts as an in-kind contribution and gets its share of the outcome. Off by default.

rows.label: WELLBYs per $1,000: HLI's conservative end

source.title: HLI report
source.quote: we estimate this project will create between 16 and 108 WELLBYs per $1,000 donated

rows.explainer: HLI: "In our conservative estimate we used our lowest reasonable guesses for these factors": how far coverage rises, how long the state would have taken without Pallium, and the effect on patients and families.

source.title: HLI report
source.quote: we estimate this project will create between 16 and 108 WELLBYs per $1,000 donated

rows.label: WELLBYs per $1,000 (geometric middle of HLI's range)
rows.explainer: HLI gives a range and no central figure. The site needs one number, so it takes the geometric mean of HLI's two ends (the middle on a ratio scale, suited to a range this wide); the choice is ours, and the sensitivity tools vary the row across HLI's range. HLI's 2025 giving season update quoted an earlier, wider range for Pallium, 26 to 163.

rows.label: Discount rate on future wellbeing
rows.explainer: The shared discount rate (Your values). HLI doesn't discount, so the evaluator view pins it at 0.

rows.label: Years over which the patients are reached

source.title: HLI report
source.quote: This project would benefit between 1.1 to 3.2 million people over the next 10 years

rows.explainer: Each patient's benefit lasts weeks, but the patients are reached over 10 years as coverage grows; we spread the WELLBYs evenly over those years. The spending comes over the first 5 years and isn't discounted, so this overstates the cut slightly (about 7% at 4%).

rows.label: Discount factor for benefits spread evenly over those years
rows.explainer: The present value of an equal benefit each year over the years above, starting now, as a share of the undiscounted total: 1 at a 0% rate, lower the longer the benefit lasts.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for research, technical assistance and policy work: mostly people. Our judgment; we haven't seen this charity's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Researchers, lawyers and advocates could typically earn considerably more in consulting, law firms or industry. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: WELLBYs per dollar
rows.explainer: The figure per dollar above; with credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
